summary: Bruno Schindler was a scholar in sinology who studied under doctoral supervisor August Conrady around 1913 to 1919. He founded Asia Major in 1923 and worked as a Verlagslektor at Lund Humphries from around 1939 to 1964.

Bryan D. Lowe is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied at Otani University and worked under advisors and teachers including Jacqueline I. Stone. He served as Assistant Professor of Religious Studies at Vanderbilt University (attested 2017–2019).

Bryan J. Cuevas works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. After undergraduate study at Emory University, he completed his PhD at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins and David Germano. He held a postdoctoral fellowship at Princeton and taught at Florida State University.

Bryan W. Van Norden specializes in philosophy and sinology. He studied at Stanford University from around 1985 to 1991 and served as a professor in the Philosophy and Chinese & Japanese departments at Vassar College from around 1996 to 2020.
Bryce Ryan was a scholar active in Indology and other fields. Over his career, he held academic posts at Cornell University and the University of Ceylon.

Bulcsu Siklós specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed a PhD at the University of London, studying under Tadeusz Skorupski and Charles R. Bawden, and held an attested post at SOAS University of London in 1996.

Bunga Fukui was a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. He studied at Waseda University and the École Pratique des Hautes Études under Paul Demiéville, Max Kaltenmark, and Rolf Alfred Stein, later serving as professor at Waseda University (~1978–2004).

Bunkyo Aoki was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University and under Kozui Otani. In 1951, he succeeded Tokan Tada as a Tibetan language lecturer at the University of Tokyo.

Bunsaku Kurata specialized in Buddhist studies, history/archaeology, and Japanology, studying at Aoyama Gakuin and Waseda University. He held posts with the National Commission for Protection of Cultural Properties, Tokyo National Museum, Agency for Cultural Affairs, and was Director of Nara National Museum.

Bunyiu Nanjio was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and sinology who studied at Oxford under Friedrich Max Müller and Arthur Anthony Macdonell. He held teaching and leadership posts at Otani University, the University of Tokyo, and Bussho Kankōkai.

Bunzaburo Matsumoto was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy who studied at the University of Tokyo. He held professorships at Rikkyo University and Kyoto University, where he also served as the second president and directed the Institute for Research in Humanities.

Burchard Brentjes was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg under Heinz Mode from 1948 to 1954, later holding a post there (~1954–1968) and succeeding Mode in 1978.

Burkhard Quessel is a Tibetology scholar who studied at the University of Hamburg. He was affiliated with the University of Hamburg (attested 1997) and served as a curator at the British Library (attested 2002–2012).

Burton Stein was a historian and Indologist. He held academic posts at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa from around 1966 to 1988 and at SOAS University of London as a Professorial Research Associate from around 1989 to 1996.

Burton Watson was a scholar of sinology and Japanology who studied at Columbia University under Wm. Theodore de Bary and at Kyoto University. He taught at Doshisha University, Kyoto University, Columbia University, and Stanford University.

Byambyn Rinchen was a scholar of linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Tibetology. He studied at the Leningrad Orient Institute and Eötvös Loránd University, and later held a post at the National University of Mongolia.

Byung-gon Kim is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied abroad at Rissho University (attested 2007). He holds a post as professor, dean, and institute director at Minobusan University (attested 2026).

C. D. Sebastian is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned his PhD at Banaras Hindu University, had postdoctoral mentorship under Paul Williams and Gavin D'Costa, and serves as Professor of Indian Philosophy at IIT Bombay (attested 2016).

C. Kunhan Raja was a scholar of Indology and philosophy who earned a D.Phil. at the University of Oxford. In 1927, he became the first University Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Madras, and later directed the Adyar Library.

C. M. Naim was a scholar in linguistics and Indology who studied at the University of California, Berkeley from around 1957 to 1960. He spent his career at the University of Chicago from around 1961 to 2001, becoming Professor Emeritus.
